page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.large is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual server from the Enhanced family, provisioned via the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8369B processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz. It allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core via hyperthreading, accompanied by 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU). The CPU features 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. Local storage is not bundled, requiring external cloud block storage for persistence, and network throughput is provisioned with a baseline of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest computational throughput constrained by the single physical core allocation. While single-core performance registers in the average band on stress-ng (1890.38) and compression tasks like gzip (28.01 GB/sec), aggregate multi-core metrics sit in lower tiers, yielding a stress-ng multi-core score of 1934.88 and a PassMark CPU score of 2992.59. Memory throughput benchmarks show 10.57 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 12.34 GB/sec for writes. The machine achieves 1.98 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 3.63 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The 1:2 core-to-memory ratio provides a low-overhead operational profile for lightweight processing tasks, making the instance a resource-efficient choice for small compute-oriented processes. The primary tradeoff stems from the limited execution resources and absence of local disks, rendering it unsuitable for data-intensive in-memory storage or high-concurrency enterprise workloads. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.large is functionally suited for lightweight microservices, basic API proxies, development sandboxes, and moderate batch utility tasks.
